t:
Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.)
Class interval | 0-5 | 5-10 | 10-15 | 15-20 | 20-25 | 25-30 | 30-35
Frequency | 3 | 5 | 4 | 2 | 7 | 6 | 5
e:
Total frequency (n): 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 32
Median position: (n/2) = 16th term
Cumulative frequencies:
0-5: 3
5-10: 8
10-15: 12
15-20: 14
20-25: 21
25-30: 27
30-35: 32
Median class: 20-25 (since 14 < 16 ≤ 21)
L = 20, F = 14, f = 7, c = 5
Median = L + ((n/2 - F) / f) X c
L- Lower limit of median class
F- Cummulative frequency
f- Freaquency of median class
c- class width
n- Total frequency.
= 20 + ((16 - 14) / 7) X 5
= 20 + (2/7) X 5
= 20 + 10/7 = 20 + 1.42857 = 21.42857
= 21.43
Option (a) is the correct answer.

t: In a seminar of 120 participants, 85 attended the morning session, 70 attended the afternoon session, and 20 attended neither. How many attended both sessions?
e: Number of participants attended at least one session = 120 - 20 = 100 Let A denotes the set of participants attended the morning session. And B denotes the set of participants attended the evening session. Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) 100 = 85 + 70 - n(A ∩ B) n(A ∩ B) = 155 - 100 n(A ∩ B) = 55 55 participants attended both sessions.

t: A person can hit a target 5 times out of 8 shots. If he fires 10 shots, what is the probability that he will hit the target twice?
e:
Probability of hitting the target P(H) = 5/8
Probability of not hitting the target P(H') = 1 - 5/8 = 3/8
If the person hit the target twice then he will not hit exactly 8 shots.
Probability that he will hit the target twice = <sup>10</sup>C<sub>2</sub> * [P(H)]<sup>2</sup> * [P(H')]<sup>8</sup>
= (10*9/2) * (5/8)<sup>2</sup> * (3/8)<sup>8</sup>
= 45 * 25 * 3<sup>8</sup>/8<sup>10</sup>
= (1125*3<sup>8</sup>)/8<sup>10</sup>

t: In a class of 60 students, 38 passed in subject A and 52 passed in subject B. If every student passed in at least one subject, how many passed in both subjects?
e: Let A represents the set of students passed in subject A and B represents the set of students passed in subject B. Then, n(A) = 38, n(B) = 52 Since everybody passed in at least one subject, n(A B) = 60 Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) 60 = 38 + 52 - n(A ∩ B) n(A ∩ B) = 90 - 60 = 30

t: At a conference of 150 attendees, 95 attended the morning workshop, 80 attended the evening workshop and 30 attended neither workshop. How many attendees attended only the evening workshop?
e: People who attended at least one workshop = 150 - 30 = 120 Using the formula, n(A B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B) At least one workshop = Morning + evening - Both 120 = 95 + 80 - Both Both = 175 - 120 = 55 Number of attendees attended only the evening workshop = Evening - Both = 80 - 55 = 25

t: The marks obtained by 15 students out of a maximum of 25 in a test are given as 13, 11, 16, 15, 18, 12, 13, 14, 10, 22, 15, 21, 20, 17 and 24. Find the product of the modes of this set of data.

t: The probabilities of solving a problem by three students A, B and C are 3/7, 5/9 and 1/5, respectively. The probability that problem will be solved is:
e:
P(A) = 3/7, P(B) = 5/9, P(C) = 1/5
Required probability = 1 - (Probability that the problem is not solved)
= 1 - P(A')P(B')P(C')
= 1 - (1 - 3/7)(1 - 5/9)(1 - 1/5)
= 1 - (4/7) * (4/9) * (4/5)
= 1 - 64/315
= 251/315

t: A speaks the truth 5 out of 7 times and B speaks truth 8 out of 9 times. What is the probability that they contradict each other in stating the same fact?
e:
P(A) = 5/7
P(B) = 8/9
Probability that A lies = 1-5/7 = 2/7
Probability that B lies = 1-8/9 = 1/9
Required probability = P(A) * P(B') + P(A') * P(B)
= (5/7) * (1/9) + (2/7) * (8/9)
= 5/63 + 16/63
= 21/63
= 1/3

If the total number of students in grade 11 was 60, all of these students opted for at least one of the three subjects mentioned here, and exactly five of these students opted for all these three subjects, what is the probability that a randomly selected student of grade 11 of this school would have opted for exactly one of these three subjects?
e:
Total number of students = 60
Number of students who opted two or more subjects = 40 + 17 + 20 + 5 - 60 = 12
Number of students who opted exactly one subject = 60 - 12 = 48
Probability = 48/60 = 0.8

t: If the difference of the mode and median of a date is 41, then the difference of the median and mean is?
e:
Given that,
Mode - Median = 41
Mode = 41 + Median
We know that,
Mode = 3 x Median - 2 x Mean
41 + Median = 3 x Median - 2 x Mean
41 = 2 x Median - 2 x Mean
Median - Mean = 41/2 = 20.5

t: A die is cast thrice and a coin is tossed thrice. Find the probability that the die will turn a 3 each time and the coin will turn a head every time.

t: If A and B are two events such that P(A ⋃ B) = 3/4, P(A ⋂ B) = 1/4 and P(B) = 1/2, then the events A and B are _____.
e:
P(A ⋃ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ⋂ B)
3/4 = P(A) + ½ - ¼
P(A) = 3/4 - ¼ = 1/2
P(A) * P(B) = 1/2 * ½ = 1/4 = P(A ⋂ B)
So, A and B are independent event.
